definition: Chronic scalp ringworm with yellow cup-shaped crusts called scutula.
Dye that colours cells so the pathologist can see them, like H&E or the Gram stain.
Fluid of plasma and cells carrying oxygen and nutrients.
Crossbar linking the two branches of an H-shaped fissure on the brain surface.
Crush syndrome: muscle trapped under rubble for hours breaks down, and freeing it floods the blood with potassium and myoglobin. Today is World Tsunami Awareness Day.

Achilles tendon: joins the calf muscles to the heel bone and is the body’s strongest tendon. A rupture mid-jump often feels like being kicked in the heel. Basketball’s inventor, Dr James Naismith, was born today in 1861.

Light Amplification by Stimulated Emission of Radiation. Lasers reshape corneas, seal leaky retinal vessels and treat skin lesions. Today is the International Day of Medical Physics, on Marie Curie’s birthday.
Kinetic energy released per unit mass: a measure of radiation dose. Fluoroscopy machines show the running air kerma, in milligray. Röntgen discovered X-rays on this day in 1895.
A test of a treatment in people. The randomised controlled trial is the gold standard. Carl Sagan, born today, would ask to see one.
Bones of the head that protect the brain.
Tissue moved from one place to another. WWI surgeon Harold Gillies rebuilt soldiers’ faces with skin grafts and flaps.
Confined to one lobe, like classic pneumococcal pneumonia.
Posterior pituitary hormone that drives labour contractions and milk let-down. Nicknamed the ‘cuddle hormone’. Happy World Kindness Day.
Cluster of pancreatic cells, beta cells included, that makes insulin.
Ridge or furrow joining two structures, e.g. the jugum sphenoidale of the skull base.
Plant roughage your gut can’t digest. Legumes, wholegrains and veg are full of it, one reason the Mediterranean diet works so well.
Pap ___: the old cervical screening test. Australia swapped it for an HPV test in 2017.
Short for Staphylococcus. The S in MRSA.
The intestines, especially the large intestine.
Organ grown during pregnancy that swaps oxygen, nutrients and waste between parent and baby through the umbilical cord. Delivered after the baby: the afterbirth.

Paul Broca, French surgeon who tied speech production to a patch of the left frontal lobe after studying a man who could say only "tan". Every hello you've said today started in his area. Today is World Hello Day.
Small lidded box that held medicines and ointments in ancient Greece. The original pill organiser, minus the days of the week.
One number divided by another, as in odds ratio or risk ratio. Divide neighbouring Fibonacci numbers and you creep towards the golden one. Today is Fibonacci Day: 1, 1, 2, 3.
Hinge joint between shin and foot, and a podiatrist's and physio's steady customer. Sprained by kerbs, netball and bad decisions on stairs.
Big flat-topped back tooth built for grinding. The first permanent ones arrive at about age six, so they've had years of your snacking.
Useful high up, unhelpful at street level: traffic fumes and sunlight make the ground-level kind, which irritates the airways. Today is World Sustainable Transport Day.

Surgery cutting connections to the brain’s frontal lobes. Egas Moniz won the 1949 Nobel Prize for it; it is now seen as one of medicine’s worst wrong turns. Alfred Nobel signed his will on this day in 1895.
Tiny pit in the centre of the macula, packed with cones and giving your sharpest vision. You're aiming it at these letters right now.
Plural of coxa: the hips, for anyone who prefers them in Latin. As in coxa vara and coxa valga.
Fungus with a talent for ruining bread. In 1928 one landed on a culture plate belonging to Scotland's Alexander Fleming, and penicillin followed. Happy St Andrew's Day.
